wordmark.purpose: "Parallax" in the header; the page's h1.

model-code.purpose: The four-letter model code in the picker, in signal ink.

model-name.purpose: The model's full name under its code.

prose.purpose: Explain notes and knob cards; capped at 80ch.

body.purpose: The model's one-line description in the picker.

label.purpose: Region titles, group and knob labels, toggles, meta. Case follows the skin's --label-case.

readout.purpose: Knob values, percentages, tempo; tabular figures.

themes.note: Landing theme. Mono throughout; scanlines on the scope; no grain.
The one light body; the signal is fill-only, text uses signal-ink.
Walnut and brass; the scope trace is a step brighter than the signal.

components.name: Signal Button
components.description: The one filled button: Surprise me.
components.css: .ds-btn-signal { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: max(11px, 0.7rem); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 5px 12px; color: var(--on-signal); background: var(--signal); border: var(--hairline-w, 1px) solid var(--signal); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); cursor: pointer; transition: filter 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-signal:hover { filter: brightness(1.1); } .ds-btn-signal:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Tool Button
components.description: Header and transport actions: Match, MIDI, Presets, Share, Play.
components.css: .ds-btn-tool { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: max(11px, 0.7rem); letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 5px 12px; color: var(--text); background: var(--surface-raised); border: var(--hairline-w, 1px) solid var(--hairline); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); cursor: pointer; transition: filter 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1), border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-tool:hover { filter: brightness(1.1); border-color: var(--signal); } .ds-btn-tool:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn-tool:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: Two to four options in a sunken track: Engine, Scope/Spectrum, Staff/Grid.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; gap: 4px; padding: 3px; background: var(--surface-sunken); border: var(--hairline-w, 1px) solid var(--hairline); border-radius: var(--radius-md); } .ds-seg-opt { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: max(11px, 0.72rem); letter-spacing: 0.03em; padding: 5px 12px; color: var(--text-muted); background: transparent; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius-sm); cursor: pointer; } .ds-seg-opt:hover { color: var(--text); background: var(--surface-raised); } .ds-seg-opt.is-on { color: var(--signal-ink); background: var(--signal-deep); border-color: var(--signal); font-weight: 600; } .ds-seg-opt:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Model List
components.description: Codes and names grouped by family; the selection reads by marker, bar and weight.
components.html: Analog & sub
components.css: .ds-list { width: 280px; background: var(--surface-sunken); border: 1px solid var(--hairline-soft); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); } .ds-fam { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: max(11px, 0.7rem); letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--text-dim); padding: 6px 10px 4px; } .ds-row { display: flex; gap: 10px; width: 100%; padding: 5px 10px; text-align: left; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--text-muted); background: none; border: 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-row:hover { color: var(--text); background: var(--surface-raised); } .ds-code { font-family: var(--font-mono); min-width: 3.5em; } .ds-row.is-sel { color: var(--text); background: var(--signal-deep); box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 var(--signal); } .ds-row.is-sel .ds-code { color: var(--signal-ink); font-weight: 600; } .ds-row.is-sel .ds-code::before { content: '▸ '; } .ds-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal); outline-offset: -2px; }

narrative.overview:
Parallax is an instrument with its cover off. While it plays, you can see what each part does: the prose under a knob rewrites itself as you turn it, the scope shows what changed, and Show me performs the control for you. The visual system exists to keep that loop legible. Nothing decorative competes with a readout, and nothing a learner needs is hidden behind a hover.

The mood is a bench instrument: precise, quiet, legible under work light. Panels are flat and divided by hairlines; corners are barely rounded; type is mostly monospaced because most of what it sets is a measurement, a code or a label. Each engine wears its own skin (a phosphor CRT for Braids, a light hardware body for Plaits, a grey console for Laxsynth, a walnut soundboard for Rings), and the skin changes when the engine does. Character comes from the skin; the chassis underneath, with its layout, components, type roles and token names, is the same for all four.

Color is held back until something is live. Idle controls sit in muted text inside hairline outlines; the signal color appears on what is selected, sounding or being turned, and always alongside a second cue a colorblind eye can read.
keyCharacteristics: Four skins on one shared token schema; the skin follows the engine, never a manual switch.
Flat panels separated by 1px hairline gaps and small tonal steps; shadows only on things that float.
Monospace for labels, codes, readouts and the Explain prose; a grotesque for names and the wordmark.
The scope is always a dark screen set into the body, even on the light Sandbox skin.
Every state survives desaturation: weight, a ▸ marker, an outline or a label carries it, and color only reinforces.

rules.name: The Second Channel Rule
rules.body: No distinction is carried by hue alone. A selected row gets a ▸ marker and an inset bar; a selected pill gets weight and an outline; an engaged knob gets a ring. Test: desaturate the screen; if two states look the same, the design is wrong.

rules.name: The Ink and Fill Rule
rules.body: `--signal` is for fills, traces and outlines. Text that wants the signal uses `--signal-ink`. In two skins they are the same value; never assume so.

rules.name: The Earned Signal Rule
rules.body: Idle controls are muted text in a hairline outline. The signal appears on what is selected, sounding or being touched, and goes away when it isn't.

rules.name: The No Wash Rule
rules.body: Translucent tints (`*-signal-deep`) may back a state that already reads without them, never carry one on their own.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text renders under 11px, on any screen. Two roles in `base.css` hold it: `--fs-label` for labels and readouts, `--fs-prose` for reading text. The floors are absolute, so a phone's smaller root size can't undercut them.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading text stops at 80ch. A wide panel gets empty space, not longer lines.

rules.name: The Explain Leads Rule
rules.body: When height is scarce, Explain keeps it. The scope has a floor (150px) and the sequencer gives way first.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels never cast shadows. If something in the frame needs to stand forward, give it a tonal step and a hairline.

dos: Do read only semantic tokens (`--signal`, `--surface-sunken`, `--text-dim`) in components; a new skin fills the schema in `tokens.css` and passes `contrast.test.ts`.
Do pair every color-coded state with weight, a marker, an outline, a label or a luminance step, and check it desaturated.
Do keep text at 11px or larger (`--fs-label`) and reading text at 13px or larger (`--fs-prose`), capped at 80ch.
Do use `--signal-ink` for any lettering in the signal color.
Do keep the scope a dark screen in every skin.
Do give touch controls at least 36px of height, and 16px text in form fields.
donts: Don't add a manual theme switcher; the skin follows the engine.
Don't set text in Sandbox's Hot Signal; it is 2.5:1 on the light body.
Don't carry meaning with a translucent tint alone.
Don't put shadows on panels inside the frame; shadows are for popovers, toasts and modals.
Don't use a colored side stripe as a card's accent; outline the whole card, as the active Explain card does.
Don't brand anything "Mutable Instruments" or "Braids"; engine names are factual labels only.
